title: The Frohmanian Symplectic Tether: Canonical Uniqueness on Coadjoint Orbits of SDiff(T3), Non-Degenerate Casimir Coupling, and Conditional Global Regularity via Quartic Young Absorption in Lean 4
description:
Conditional result. Not a Clay Millennium claim. Nothing in this record proves global regularity for the 3D Navier–Stokes equations.

Product theorem (FinalProductTheorem.lean): frohmanian_metriplectic_system_canonical_uniqueness_and_global_regularity_product_theorem (hκ : 0 < kappa) : P1_CanonicalFiveStepUniqueness kappa ∧ P2_MetriplecticSplitAndCasimirDamping kappa ∧ P3_QuarticYoungAbsorption kappa ∧ P4_UnconditionalLyapunovCeiling. κ is a positive parameter; the value 27CCZ4/(4ν3) appears only as motivation in the paper and is not formalized. The four conjuncts, as defined in the Lean:

  • P1: every symmetric bilinear correction B that is coadjoint-invariant (C1), degenerate with respect to the kinetic energy (C2), gives controllable negative feedback (C3), saturates the tether quadratic and polarizes (with Polarizes (TetherKernel kappa) also assumed) equals TetherKernel kappa (this conjunct appears twice, from uniqueness_of_minimal_tether and uniqueness_of_minimal_symmetric_tether); every B with kernel density equal to the canonical density −κ‖ω(x)‖2 equals TetherKernel kappa; and TetherKernel kappa scales by c2 under ω ↦ cω (c ≠ 0) when the functional derivatives are scale-invariant.
  • P2: the KKS form is skew; the pointwise cyclic Jacobi identity holds; the metriplectic pairing on the diagonal equals TetherKernel and is ≤ 0; the tethered bracket with the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian equals the classical bracket under the stated identity, divergence-free and integrability hypotheses; Pi_u u (λ u) = 0 when ∫‖u‖2 ≠ 0; and the pointwise tether density is < 0 where ω(x) ≠ 0 and Pi_u of the functional derivative is nonzero.
  • P3: an algebraic Young-absorption step (if 4CCZM I4 ≤ (κ/4)I6 + CabsM3φ3/2 and I6 ≥ 0, then subtracting κI6 leaves −(3/4)κI6); sup-norm pinning at an attained maximum; a pointwise Bochner–polar viscous damping inequality from stated derivative data; and the near/far cutoff inequality from stated bounds. The Young bound itself is a hypothesis.
  • P4: a scalar ODE fact: for C, κ'' > 0, every y : ℝ → ℝ differentiable on [0, ∞) with y' ≤ Cy2 − κ''y3 there satisfies y(t) ≤ max(y(0), C/κ'') for t ≥ 0. That an actual Navier–Stokes vorticity obeys this inequality is not proved.

The Lean docstrings mark P1, P2 and this product theorem as scaffolding for the ψ-slot tether: C2 fails for that form on an explicit shear (shear_C2_fails), so the C1–C3 hypothesis class in P1 may be empty for κ ≠ 0, in which case those conjuncts hold vacuously (not settled by a Lean theorem here). The velocity-slot model is TetherKernelVel with velocity_tether_product_theorem (P1Vel ∧ P2Vel ∧ P3 ∧ P4, assuming κ ≥ 0).

Navier–Stokes statement is conditional. global_regularity_for_NS (GlobalRegularity.lean) gives a global smooth solution for smooth, divergence-free, finite-energy u0 and ν > 0 assuming the open time-uniform vorticity bound FrohmanianTetherBound and the local-theory hypotheses KatoLocalWitness (local existence), PhysicalBKMContinuationCriterionFor (Beale–Kato–Majda continuation) and KatoUniquenessOnExistenceTimes (uniqueness), none of which is proved here; they are discharged only at u0 ≡ 0 (global_regularity_for_NS_nonvacuous_at_zero). Earlier versions of this record claimed a fifth component, that every physical flow of the tethered dynamics extends smoothly to all times; no such theorem exists and that claim is withdrawn.

Model caveat. The spatial type T3 is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), i.e. ℝ3 with Lebesgue measure, not the torus. The L2 hypothesis ∫ℝ3‖u0‖2 < ∞ forces any Z3-periodic datum to be zero, so global_regularity_for_NS does not model genuine periodic data. Code comments saying that smooth data on T3 are automatically integrable are wrong in this encoding.
